To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
signaling at the orexin receptor 1 is involved in pronounced self-administration of sucrose and in reinstatement of sucrocse-seeking elicited by cues in food-restricted male rats.
orexin receptor signaling is involved in pronounced food reward and cue-induced reinstatement during food restriction.
orexin/hypothalamic arousal system signaling is involved in the motivation to seek food rewards during food restriction, as well as cue-induced reinstatement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological mechanisms that regulate food intake, with an emphasis on the role of orexin/hypocretin in food-seeking behavior.
the role of orexin/hypercretin in food-seeking and food-restriction.
understanding the neurobiological basis of the reinforcing effects of food, with the ultimate goal of developing new treatments for eating disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the orexin system is involved in the motivational properties of food reward, and that this involvement is increased during food restriction.
the Orexin system is strongly involved in food reward seeking, particularly in food restriction.
orexin/hypothalamic signaling is involved in food reward-seeking and reinstatement of reward-seeking during food restriction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Orx system is a critical regulator of food-seeking during food restriction.
the Orexin system is strongly engaged during periods when food rewards are highly salient, such as when food is restricted.
the Orx system is strongly engaged by food restriction and by cues associated with food restriction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
food restriction increases the motivation for food rewards, which is reflected in the increased expression of the Orx system in response to food cues.
Orx system is involved in cue-induced reinstating of extinguished sucrocse-seeking, but not sucrose self-administion.
Orx signaling in the hypothalamus is involved in food reward seeking in food-restricted animals, and this is especially the case for food-paired cues.
